title: Excess count detection for epidemiological time series
text: Excess count detection (excode) epidemiological time series important part public health surveillance systems. variety algorithms developed identify events disease outbreaks excess mortality. end, time series analysed detect unusually large (case) counts, exceed normally expected certain time period geographical region. normal expectancy cases current time period usually calculated based historic data. excode package provides flexible framework implements extends well established approaches control seasonality, long-term trends historic events, also allows use customized models. user can choose Poisson Negative Binomial distribution, commonly used probability distributions modeling count data. combining hidden Markov models generalized linear models, excode explicitly models normally expected case counts expected excess case counts, .e. time point time series labeled either normal state excess state. detailed overview excess count detection available methods, recommend surveillance package.

title: Excess count detection for epidemiological time series
text: Many epidemiological times series public health interest show periodic changes cases depending seasons calendar periods. Seasonal patterns can modeled excode follows: Mean: model account seasonal cyclical patterns. expectancy normal excess case counts modeled mean historic data. FarringtonNoufaily: popular algorithm, models seasonality segmenting year predefined number shorter time periods, different expectancy observed cases. Harmonic: ‘Harmonic’ model uses sine cosine functions account seasonal cyclical patterns data. Custom: ‘Custom’ model allows user define model providing data.frame containing covariate data.

what: Using excode for excess count detection
title: Excess count detection for epidemiological time series
text: input data data.frame least two variables containing dates observed number cases: date: date (time period) event, e.g. reporting date, date disease onset date death. observed: observed number cases. Optional variables : offset: e.g. susceptible population. state: numeric vector labels time points known ‘normal’ state, set 0=normal NA=unknown. shadar_df contains number weekly cases Salmonella hadar 2001 2006 Germany (taken surveillance package). excode applied data using ‘Poisson’ distribution two states, ‘Harmonic’ model ‘Linear’ time trend. Excess count detection carried using run_excode() function. time points excess expected rare (e.g. disease outbreak detection) recommended set set_baseline_state = TRUE. assigns low case counts ‘normal’ state initialization improves model fitting. model estimated run_excode() multiple time points: 209 - 295. Results can extracted using summary() function: result data.frame following variables: posterior0: Probability ‘normal’ state . posterior1: Probability ‘excess’ state. pval: P-value null hypothesis excess current timepoint. zscore: Measures many standard deviations observed number cases mu0. value 2.33 corresponds p-value 0.01. date: event date (e.g. reporting date date disease onset). timepoint: Timepoint (integer) time series. observed: Number cases. mu0: Number expected cases ‘normal’ state. mu1: Number expected cases ‘excess’ state. BIC: Bayesian information criterion. AIC: Aikake information criterion. model two states, columns showing respective posterior mu values. result summary can visualised using plot_excode_summary() function. Figure 1 shows cyclical pattern case counts, cases summer fewer cases cases winter. outbreak lead surge case numbers 2006 compared previous years. Figure 1: Weekly Salmonella Hadar cases fitted ‘normal’ (mu0) ‘excess’ (mu1) state means. Bottom panels show posterior probability excess case counts, z-scores -log10(p-value) detected excess case counts three measures selected cutoffs. Models ‘Mean’ ‘FarringtonNoufaily’ can applied likewise.
code: library(excode) ## Load data and show first 6 rows data("shadar_df") kable(as_tibble(shadar_df[1:6, ])) %>%   kable_styling(font_size = 11) result_shadar_har <- run_excode(     surv_ts = shadar_df,     timepoints = 209:295,     distribution = "Poisson",     states = 2,     periodic_model = "Harmonic",     time_trend = "Linear",     set_baseline_state = TRUE ) summary_shadar_har <- summary(result_shadar_har) kable(as_tibble(summary_shadar_har[82:87, ])) %>%   kable_styling(font_size = 11) # Add historic data shadar_plot <- shadar_df %>%    dplyr::filter(!date %in% summary_shadar_har$date &                    lubridate::year(shadar_df$date)>=2003)%>%    bind_rows(summary_shadar_har)  # Plot results for time points 209-295 with historic data plot_excode_summary(shadar_plot, type="bar")

what: A short overview of the statistical model
title: Excess count detection for epidemiological time series
text: excode package combines Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) Hidden Markov Models (HMMs). GLM part model allows use regression models model seasonal patterns general trends time series. Additionally, algorithm excess count detection needs account excess counts historic data used model estimation. HMM part statistical model used excode allows explicitly consider past disease outbreaks model. HMM separates time series two () states: normal state one (multiple) excess state. normal state, observed case counts lie within range normally expected certain time period. excess state, case counts higher normally expected, .e. potential outbreak excess mortality. contrast algorithms used excess count detection, either account previous excess case counts use heuristic -weighting past instances excess counts. simplicity, consider two state model ‘normal’ state \(N\) ‘excess’ state \(E\). position \(t\) time series length \(T\) state \(s_t \\left\{ N,E\right\}, t\\left[1;T\right]\) , \(N\) represents normal \(E\) excess state. sequence normal excess states modeled HMM using initial state transition probabilities: Initial state probabilities \(\Pr(s_{1}=N\bigr)\) \(\Pr(s_{1}=E\bigr)\) give probability first time point time series respective state. Transition probabilities give probability time point \(t\) specific state, given state previous time point. instance, \(\Pr\left(s_{t}=N\left|s_{t-1}=N\right.\right)\), \(t\\left[1;T\right]\) gives probability time series normal state time point \(t\), given position \(t-1\) also normal state. \(\Pr\left(s_{t}=E\left|s_{t-1}=N\right.\right)\) gives probability transition excess state time point \(t\), given \(t-1\) normal state. expected case counts position \(t\), \(\mu_t\), can modeled using GLM sine cosine functions control seasonal patterns (one models available excode): \[ \log\mu_{t}=\beta_{0}+\beta_{1}t+ \beta_3 \cos(\frac{2\pi}{52}t) + \beta_4\sin(\frac{2\pi}{52}t) + \beta_{5}\left(s_{t}=E\right) \] , \(\beta_{0}\) intercept, \(\beta_{1}t\) linear time trend, \(\beta_3\) \(\beta_4\) model seasonal patterns using \(\sin\) \(\cos\) functions weekly data (52 time points per year). increase cases incorporated \(\beta_{5}\). Based model, excode calculates probability excess case counts current time point - posterior probability. Moreover, given normally expected case counts model, p-value null hypothesis, excess current timepoint calculated. z-score calculated based quasi-Poisson regression similar EuroMOMO.

One columns named mu0, mu1, … model fits. states Optional integer giving number latent states (.e., many mu* series consider). missing, inferred available columns matching "^mu\d+$". provided, mu0 mu{states-1} exist excode_summary used. posterior_cutoff Numeric \([0,1]\). Horizontal reference line threshold excess probability panel (default 0.5). zscore_cutoff Numeric. Horizontal reference line threshold z-score panel (default 2). p_cutoff Numeric \((0,1]\). Transformed \(-\log_{10}\) p-value panel used threshold tiles (default 0.025). type Character, either "line" "bar" (partial matching disabled via match.arg). Controls whether panels drawn ribbons/lines ("line") columns ("bar"). first panel, "bar" draws observed bars mu* steps; "line" draws series lines.

title: Plot EXCODE summary diagnostics across multiple panels — plot_excode_summary
text: Missing values handled defensively plotting: posterior0 = 1 (excess), zscore = 0, pval = 1. consistent black/green/orange-red palette used first panel: observed black; mu0 green; remaining mu* gold tomato. Facet strips placed right common theme applied panels align cleanly combined patchwork. final plot stacks five panels (top bottom): Observed counts model fits. Excess probability \(1 - \mathrm{posterior0}\) dotted cutoff. z-score dotted cutoff (ribbon handles positive/negative). \(-\log_{10}(p)\) dotted cutoff \(-\log_{10}(\mathrm{p\_cutoff})\). Binary “tiles” summarizing whether metric exceeds cutoff.

title: Detect excess counts in epidemiological time series — run_excode
text: surv_ts data.frame surveillance time series described Details. timepoints Integer integer vector time points perform detection; must provided unless embedded MultiState formula. time_units_back Integer number past time units used fitting (interpreted relative timepoints_per_unit model’s excodeFormula); default 5. distribution Character emission family passed excodeFamily(), e.g., "Poisson" "NegBinom". states Integer (>= 2) number latent states initialization/fitting. time_trend Character time-trend specification forwarded excodeFormula(), one c("Linear","Spline1","Spline2","Spline3","Spline4","None"); default "None". periodic_model Character background model name forwarded excodeFormula(), one c("Mean","FarringtonNoufaily","Harmonic","Custom"); default "Harmonic". period_length Integer number time points per unit season used timepoints_per_unit excodeFormula() (e.g., 52 weekly per year, 365 daily per year); default 52. intercept Logical; include intercept constructed formulas; default TRUE. covariate_df data.frame NULL; optional covariates used constructing excodeFormula(); default NULL. weights_threshold Numeric SD cutoff surveillance::algo.farrington.assign.weights() -weighting residuals baseline refit; default 2.58. weights_threshold_baseline Numeric Anscombe residual cutoff used mark non-baseline points clustering initialization; default 1. set_baseline_state Logical; TRUE, compute/assign background state initialization; default FALSE. maxIter Integer maximum number EM iterations; default 100. verbose Logical; print progress; default FALSE. return_full_model Logical; FALSE (default) return results requested timepoints; TRUE, return full time series used fitting timepoint.

title: Detect excess counts in epidemiological time series — run_excode
text: fitted excodeModel containing, requested time points (full series return_full_model = TRUE), posterior state probabilities, fitted means, p-values, Anscombe residuals, convergence information, information criteria.

title: Detect excess counts in epidemiological time series — run_excode
text: input surv_ts must data.frame columns: date (aggregation date), observed (case counts), optional offset (e.g., population risk), optional state (e.g., 0 = background, 1 = excess, NA = unknown). Passing sts objects (surveillance), lists sts, matrix-like collections sts supported. model’s emission uses MultiState excodeFormula already contains surv_ts slot, run_excode() uses data , missing, sets timepoints accordingly.

title: Summary of an excodeModel — summary,excodeModel-method
text: object excodeModel summarize. pars Character vector fields include (e.g., "posterior", "pval", "zscore", "date", "timepoint", "observed", "emission", "BIC", "AIC"); defaults . prob_threshold Numeric posterior probability threshold used compute posterior-based upper bound (posterior_ub) flag excess counts (>= threshold); default 0.5. pval_threshold Numeric p-value threshold used compute p-value-based upper bound (pval_ub) flag excess counts (<= threshold); default 0.01. anscombe_threshold Numeric threshold Anscombe z-score used signal assessment; default 2. maxiter Integer maximum iterations estimating posterior alarm threshold; default 1000.
